newsitem.title: USA: Gensia to restructure spin off R&D operations.
newsitem.headline: Gensia to restructure spin off R&D operations.

text.p: Struggling biotechnology company Gensia Inc. said Tuesday it will spin off virtually all its research and development operations and realign as an integrated manufacturer and supplier of cancer chemotherapy drugs.

The sweeping restructuring will involve Gensia's purchase of three foreign pharmaceutical companies, which it will pay for by issuing 29.5 million new common shares. Based on the company's closing share price Tuesday, before the restructuring was announced, the deal has a value of about $158.6 million.
In the second part of the deal, Gensia said it will spin off its extensive research and development operations into a newly formed public company, to be called Metabasis Therapeutics Inc.
The company's decision to essentially exit the drug R&D business follows two years of struggling to rebound from the setback dealt when its lead drug candidate was found to be ineffective.

In October 1994, the company's stock price was cut in half after it found its Protara drug candidate, which had been expected to generate hundreds of millions of dollars in sales by the end of the decade, was not viable.
The drug had been designed to reduce the risk of heart attack, stroke, or cardiac death in patients undergoing coronary bypass surgery.
Gensia's stock, which was trading at over $10 a share before the Protara setback, has recovered virtually none of its value in the two years since then.
"(Gensia) has not made any bones about the fact that R&D was not something they could afford to continue," said Mehta and Isaly analyst Viren Mehta.

The planned restructuring will be accomplished through the purchase of SICOR SpA, a Milan-based supplier of specialty bulk pharmaceuticals; Sintesis Lerma SA de CV, a Mexican supplier of specialty bulk pharmaceuticals; and Lemery SA de CV, a multisource pharmaceutical company based in Mexaco that sells to markets in Central and South America and Eastern Europe.
The companies being purchased had combined annual sales in the first six months of 1996 of $36.4 million, while Gensia's in the same period totaled $25.7 million.

The new company will be called Gensia Sicor Inc. and will remain based in San Diego. Sicor and Lerma will produce and sell bulk specialty drugs to pharmaceutical companies around the world and Lemery and Gensia Laboratories Ltd. will handle formulation, filling, packaging and marketing of multisource injectable drugs.
